speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have significant symptoms including fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To narrow this down, are you experiencing any fever or loss of appetite, and do you have a history of recent infections or travel?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Have you noticed any specific abdominal symptoms like jaundice, changes in stool color, or blood in your stool, and do you have any history of liver disease?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), LDH, and ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of the abdomen and neck.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (specifically, consider Hodgkin Lymphoma or Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma). The combination of B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and elevated LDH/ESR strongly suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder. I recommend proceeding with a biopsy of the enlarged lymph node for definitive confirmation.
